sections.heading: Safe driving tips — B
sections.markdown:
Audience and scope: safe driving tips within the selected first-time passenger-car knowledge preparation path. This is an authoring scope from the pinned run configuration.
Coverage plan: Visual search and speed; Water and stopping distance; Space around the vehicle; Communicating movements; Preventing hot-vehicle injuries. These are authored organizational labels, with no official examination weighting or eligibility assertion.
Visual search, speed adjustment, curves, slippery roads, water hazards, all stopping and following values, side and rear space, horns, signals and hot-vehicle prevention are represented. The externally attributed annual child-death count is withheld because its original authority is not verified. No blanket legal immunity is claimed for rescue. The slide-braking statement conflicts with the winter section's no-braking instruction and remains review debt.

sections.heading: Safe driving tips — C
sections.markdown:
FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A59
Use a consistent search pattern to notice developing problems early enough to change speed or road position. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A60
Ideally scan the intended route twenty to thirty seconds ahead to see traffic and plan adjustments. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A60
Look to the sides for traffic crossing your path and over your shoulders toward the rear to check blind spots. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A60
Check rear traffic in the mirrors, especially before changing lanes, slowing, stopping or entering an intersection. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A60
Adjust speed to road and traffic conditions while maintaining sufficient following space and obeying applicable speed limits. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A60
Slow before a curve to a speed that permits light, steady acceleration through it. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A60
Reduce curve speed further when grip is poor, when following another vehicle or when the curve's end is hidden. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A60
Slow at the first indication of rain, snow, sleet or ice. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A60
Reduced tire grip on slippery pavement increases stopping distance and makes turning without a skid harder. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A60
The safe-driving section describes slowly releasing the accelerator and gently applying the brake when a vehicle begins to slide. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A60
On wet, snowy or icy pavement, slow down and increase the gap behind the vehicle ahead. [A60]
Source: [A60 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A61
Hydroplaning happens when the steering tires ride over pooled water instead of gripping the roadway. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A61
Slow down in rain and on wet roads containing pooled water or puddles to reduce hydroplaning traction loss. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A61
If hydroplaning occurs, ease off the accelerator slowly. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A61
Do not drive through a large area of standing road water; choose a different route around flooding. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A61
A space cushion is the gap kept between your vehicle and other road users that gives you time to respond. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A61
Stopping distance covers the vehicle's movement from recognizing a need to stop until the vehicle is stationary under ideal conditions. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A61
Higher travel speed requires more time and distance to stop. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A61
Perception time covers recognizing that a stop is needed, with an alert driver's stated average ranging from three quarters of a second to one second. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A62
Reaction time covers moving from accelerator to brake and beginning to brake, with the stated average ranging from three quarters of a second to one second. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A62
At fifty miles per hour on dry pavement with good brakes, the handbook gives about one hundred fifty-eight feet as a possible braking distance. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A62
The handbook recommends at least one vehicle length per ten miles per hour of speed, or a four-second gap behind the vehicle ahead. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A62
Start counting when the leading vehicle's rear passes a fixed landmark and continue until your vehicle reaches that same landmark. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A62
Reaching the chosen landmark before four seconds have elapsed means you are following too closely under the stated interval method. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A62
If the interval is too short, reduce speed and measure again at another fixed point until the gap is at least four seconds. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A62
Practice estimating the seconds to an object, then count the actual travel time to compare your estimate. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A62
Increase front space at night or whenever weather limits visibility. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A62
Increase the following distance on slippery pavement. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A62
Increase the following gap behind trucks, buses, recreational vehicles and vehicles towing trailers. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A62
Leave more following space behind vehicles required to stop at railroad tracks, such as buses or hazardous-material carriers. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0062]

sections.heading: Safe driving tips — C2
sections.markdown:
FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A62
Space beside the vehicle provides room to move right or left to avoid a crash. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A62
Avoid staying next to another vehicle for long periods because you may occupy its blind spot and lose room for an evasive move. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A63
Avoid hugging the centerline and maximize the separation from oncoming traffic. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A63
Help vehicles entering a multilane or limited-access road by changing lanes or adjusting speed to create room. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A63
Give extra room to pedestrians, particularly children, and to bicycle riders. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A63
As a tractor-trailer passes, move toward the outer part of your own lane to leave a little more clearance from it. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A63
Help traffic behind maintain space by keeping speed steady, signaling early and adding front space before slowing or turning. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A63
Use headlights from sunset to sunrise, in poor visibility and whenever precipitation requires windshield-wiper use. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A63
High beams may be used when headlights are needed except when oncoming traffic approaches. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A63
Use a light horn tap to attract attention when pedestrians or cyclists approach your lane, when a vehicle you are passing begins moving into it, or when a driver seems unaware of you. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R11 | anchor: A63
Use the horn only for necessary communication because inappropriate use may frighten or anger another road user. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R12 | anchor: A64
Signal for a lane change, merge or turn so other road users have time to respond. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R13 | anchor: A64
Activate a turn signal at least one hundred feet before the intended turn. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R14 | anchor: A64
Cancel the turn signal after the maneuver to avoid confusing other drivers. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R15 | anchor: A64
Brake lights tell other road users that the vehicle is slowing or stopping. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R16 | anchor: A64
Signal before slowing to turn off a road without a separate turn or exit lane, or to park or turn before an intersection. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R17 | anchor: A64
Never leave children alone inside or around cars. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R18 | anchor: A64
Make a habit of checking the rear seat before locking the vehicle. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R19 | anchor: A65
An item needed at your destination can be placed in the rear seat as a reminder to check there. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R20 | anchor: A65
A stuffed animal on the front passenger seat can serve as a visual reminder to check for a child. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R21 | anchor: A65
Ask the childcare provider to contact you if your child does not arrive as expected. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R22 | anchor: A65
Keep a year-round habit of locking vehicle doors and the trunk, and encourage caregivers, friends and neighbors to do the same. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R23 | anchor: A65
If a child is missing, inspect nearby vehicles' passenger areas and trunks even when locked, because a child may have locked the doors from inside. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R24 | anchor: A65
If a child is alone in a vehicle, immediately call nine one one while checking for an unlocked door and trying to find the parent. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R25 | anchor: A65
The handbook directs removal of a distressed or unresponsive child from the vehicle, including breaking a window if necessary. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R26 | anchor: A65
Stay with the child until emergency help arrives. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R27 | anchor: A65
Do not leave pets in a vehicle; the handbook states that even cracked windows can allow a twenty-degree Fahrenheit rise in ten minutes. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0065]

Confusables: perception, reaction and braking describe different parts of stopping; hydroplaning is tires riding over pooled water. A rear-seat reminder does not replace checking the seat. Mnemonic: search, space, signal. Glossary: space cushion is response room around the vehicle; following interval is the timed front gap. These cues add no new physical or legal claims.
